name: Jahath
overview: Jahath was a male member of the tribe of Levi, specifically identified as the son of Gershom. He belonged to the Gershonite clan, descendants of Gershon, who was one of Levi's sons. This lineage places Jahath within the Levitical family responsible for particular religious duties in Israel.
namesAndTitles: The name Jahath means 'snatch up' in Hebrew. It is a proper name recorded in Scripture but is not indicated to have been given directly by God. This meaning may reflect a characteristic or role, though the biblical text does not elaborate further.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records that Jahath was the son of Gershom. It is also inferred that Shimei was his father, suggesting a generational link within the Gershonite family. Beyond these, no additional family relationships are documented.
scriptureSignificance: Jahath's significance lies in his position within the Levitical genealogy as a Gershonite, connecting him to the tribe entrusted with sacred duties in Israel. His identification as the son of Gershom highlights the continuity of Levitical service through generations. Although not prominent in narrative events, his mention preserves the genealogical record essential for understanding the organization and heritage of the Levites.
